parallel.requirements: Recognized the full OS lab: projects P1 through P6 with exact required function signatures, and by round 3 still had P4, P5, and P6 in the remaining set.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used commits for early projects, then assigned P4 review/commit, P5 review/commit, P6 implementation tasks and launched a broad P4/P5 adversarial workflow.
parallel.implementation: Completed and committed P1 through P3; drafted P4/P5/P6 workspace changes but late round work centered on fixing P5 net and memory findings from the workflow.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final git history only contains requirement commits through p3_process_management, while P4/P5/P6 task records remained pending or in progress.
parallel.verification: Ran builds and a large verifier workflow; official evaluation completed and failed with 117 passed and 18 failed raw final-test entries.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: P4/P5/P6 were not committed as requirement deliverables, P5 still had at least one failing MM test, and P6 filesystem functions remained incomplete at timeout.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same seven-project OS task and entered round 3 with P5 and P6 still remaining after committing P4 in round 2.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked locally without child agents or workflows, proceeding from P5 scheduler/MM/network fixes to P6 filesystem edits.
serial.implementation: Committed P1 through P5, including P5 device-driver changes, then started P6 filesystem header and implementation work before timeout.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The git history includes impl: p5_device_driver above impl: p4_virtual_memory, but no completed P6 requirement commit was produced.
serial.verification: Used local builds and host tests without delegation; official evaluation completed and failed with 109 passed and 26 failed raw final-test entries.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: P6 remained incomplete and several earlier scheduler/VM expanded checks still failed in the official evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run had the full seven-requirement RISC-V OS task and in round 3 still had P4, P5, and P6 as tracked remaining work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had the same prompt and entered round 3 with P5 and P6 remaining after P4 had been completed in round 2.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the same task surface, but serial had reduced the remaining committed requirement set before the last round while parallel still had three uncommitted requirements.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel round 3 split work into P4 review/commit, P5 review/commit, P6 implementation, and a separate P4/P5 adversarial workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial round 3 proceeded in one local line of work: port and fix P5, commit it, then start surveying and editing P6.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced extra ownership and review breadth around P4/P5 while serial kept the critical path sequential and moved from P5 to P6 after a commit.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel transferred review findings back to the parent, and the parent explicitly read and reduced them to seven confirmed P5 findings.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept context local; when an edit failed because a file had not been read, it read the file and retried the edit directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The key context difference was volume and coordination overhead, not missing context: parallel consumed a large returned review bundle, while serial used local file context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent the late round fixing P5 network and memory defects after review, with edits still occurring at the end of the agent window.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ported scheduler and memory pieces into P5, fixed a flush issue, committed P5, and began P6 filesystem implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was still remediating P5 defects near timeout, whereas serial turned P5 into a committed requirement and shifted effort to P6.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The P4/P5 verifier workflow completed and returned; the parent inspected it, but the tracked P4 and P5 commit tasks remained pending and P6 in progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle, with workflows and delegation disabled and no workflow child logs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not lose the verifier result, but processing that result displaced closure; serial avoided that lifecycle cost entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel left the git history at the P3 commit even though later P4/P5/P6 workspace edits existed, so requirement-patch integration was not closed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial git history includes an `impl: p5_device_driver` commit above the P4 commit, showing P5 integration into the required delivery workflow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The divergence is not a write collision; it is that parallel failed to package late integrated work into requirement commits while serial did so through P5.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used local builds and a verifier workflow, then official evaluation still failed P4/P5/P6 cases even though many P6 cases passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial official evaluation shows the P5 expanded and output tests passing, but many P6 filesystem tests failing after only beginning P6 edits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more review evidence but insufficient closure; serial had less workflow verification but a cleaner P5 acceptance state and weaker P6 completion.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel round 3 used a workflow with 70 child logs in status, 3070614 workflow-child tokens, 966 child tool calls, and timed out with P4/P5/P6 still tracked unfinished.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial round 3 had workflows disabled, zero workflow child tokens and zero workflow tasks, then timed out after committing P5 and starting P6.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The retained coordination difference is late broad fan-out budget exhaustion in parallel versus serial local progression through P5 before P6 timeout.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status evaluations mark both modes as failed, so this pair is both_fail rather than a discordant official outcome. The concrete task-solving difference is closure order: parallel used late P4/P5 review fan-out, consumed substantial child-agent budget, then was still repairing P5 and left P4/P5/P6 requirement commits unfinished; serial worked locally, committed P5, then began P6 and failed with broader P6 incompleteness. The raw evaluator counts favor parallel on total passing tests, but the official relation remains both_fail.
parallel_contributors: Late broad P4/P5 workflow fan-out consumed a large share of the final round and shifted the parent back to P5 fixes near timeout.
Parallel final git history stopped at p3_process_management despite later workspace edits and partial P6 functionality.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one local path through P5 and committed impl: p5_device_driver before starting P6.
Serial avoided child-result lifecycle overhead but still timed out with P6 filesystem incomplete.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts retained ordinary implementation defects in scheduler and VM functions, and both failed P6 filesystem coverage.
Parallel raw final-test entries passed more P6 checks than serial, while serial had cleaner committed P5 requirement accounting.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No pass/fail outcome difference; the retained pattern explains an adverse parallel closure process, not a discordant official result.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent launched a broad P4/P5 adversarial review workflow late in round 3 while P6 implementation and P4/P5 commits remained. The workflow generated 41 child-agent records and consumed 3070614 child tokens and 966 child tool calls; after it returned, the parent was still triaging seven P5 findings and editing P5 within seconds of timeout, leaving tracked requirement commits unfinished.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The finite round-3 closure window was spent absorbing and fixing review findings, leaving P4/P5/P6 task records unfinished and no P4/P5/P6 requirement commits in the parallel git history before timeout.
